expect: 306 mAh/gS and 87 mAh/g electrode (p5.L103-105): ratio 28.4%; the stated loading is 35 wt% sulfur (in the carbon-sulfur composite)
question: After 1500 cycles, what capacity does the cathode deliver per gram of sulfur and per gram of the whole electrode, and what sulfur share of the electrode does their ratio imply, against the sulfur content the paper states?
rendered:
According to the document, after 1500 cycles at 1C rate, the cathode delivers 306 mAh/gS capacity per gram of sulfur. The capacity per gram of the whole electrode is 87 mAh/g.

To find the sulfur share of the electrode, we can calculate the ratio of the capacity per gram of sulfur to the capacity per gram of the whole electrode:

(306 mAh/gS) / (87 mAh/g) = 3.52 gS/g electrode

The paper states that the sulfur content is 35 wt % (or 35/100 = 0.35 gS/g electrode). This is lower than the calculated sulfur share of 3.52 gS/g electrode, which is expected since the capacity per gram of the whole electrode is less than the theoretical capacity per gram of sulfur.
